statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-70159 (GHSA-334f-vvp4-7g6p) is an ASP.NET Core SignalR denial of service issue: stateful reconnect clients can block broadcasts indefinitely through MessageBuffer.ResendAsync backpressure and keep the associated resources alive. Microsoft lists Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Common as affected from 10.0.0 through 10.0.12 and fixed in 10.0.13, names Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Core as the other affected library, and lists Windows, Linux and macOS as affected platforms (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-334f-vvp4-7g6p, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/452, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.13/10.0.13.md). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's dotnet/dotnet source release, and each build's version is the .NET release it carries. Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0, 10.0.3-r0, 10.0.4-r0, 10.0.5-r0, 10.0.6-r0, 10.0.7-r0, 10.0.8-r0, 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold. Implementation copies of Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Common.dll and Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Core.dll are in the Microsoft.AspNetCore.App shared framework (aspnetcore10-runtime, and the .NET SDK held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap) and in the ASP.NET Core runtime pack and runtime archive in dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap, and SignalR.Common is also in the Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Common nupkg in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts; the other copies are reference assemblies with no implementation code. Every implementation copy carries the build's own .NET version, on both architectures, so the copies in the first nine builds (10.0.2-r0 to 10.0.10-r0) are unfixed and every copy from 10.0.13-r0 on is 10.0.13 or later. The range ends at 10.0.13-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-70159 (GHSA-334f-vvp4-7g6p) is an ASP.NET Core denial of service issue in SignalR: clients using stateful reconnect can block broadcasts indefinitely through MessageBuffer.ResendAsync backpressure and keep the associated resources. Microsoft lists the Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Common package as affected from 8.0.0 through 8.0.31 and fixed in 8.0.32, on Windows, Linux and macOS (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-334f-vvp4-7g6p, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/452, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.32/8.0.32.md). DHI dotnet8-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 8 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 220 packages of the ten published builds (8.0.23-r0, 8.0.24-r0, 8.0.25-r0, 8.0.26-r0, 8.0.27-r0, 8.0.29-r0, 8.0.31-r0, 8.0.32-r0, 8.0.33-r0 and 8.0.34-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold: every build ships Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Common.dll and Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Core.dll at its own .NET version, in the ASP.NET Core shared framework of aspnetcore8-runtime and of the .NET SDK held by dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap and in the ASP.NET Core runtime pack held by dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap, and Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Common.dll also in the Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Common nupkg in dotnet8-runtime-artifacts, plus reference assemblies with no implementation code (including 6.0.2 reference assemblies in source-build reference packages): 8.0.23 to 8.0.31 in the first seven builds and 8.0.32 or later from 8.0.32-r0 on. The range ends at 8.0.32-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.
